title: ci-cd rollback breadcrumbs - canary fail notes
content:
Context:
- Canary deployment (frontend-inference-service) for release v2025.02.14-rc3 started 2025-02-18 09:10 PST.
- Goal: push latency-optimizations patch (reworked batching + kernel selector tweak) behind feature flag and verify at 2% traffic.
- Canary failed: elevated 50th/95th latency, some 502/503 responses from the runtime, spike in token generation errors.

Timeline & commands tried (breadcrumbs):
- 2025-02-18 09:10 - started canary via helm:
  $ helm upgrade --install frontend-inference ./charts/frontend --namespace prod --set image.tag=v2025.02.14-rc3 --set canary.enabled=true --set canary.weight=2
  -> helm returned SUCCESS, rollout triggered.

- 2025-02-18 09:22 - observed first errors in canary logs (via kubectl):
  $ kubectl -n prod logs deploy/frontend-inference-canary -c runtime | tail -n 50\  
  2025-02-18T09:21:57Z ERROR inference/runtime - kv-cache miss after recompile, falling back to cold path
  2025-02-18T09:21:57Z WARN  http.server - upstream response 502 (upstream: runtime-process-xx)
  2025-02-18T09:22:03Z ERROR model-loader - incompatible operator: scaled_attention_softmax_v2

- 2025-02-18 09:25 - ran smoke curl against canary endpoint (2% traffic LB):
  $ curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...' -d '{"model":"openlm-rewrite","input":"hello"}'
  HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
  Content-Type: application/json
  {"error":"upstream runtime error: op_scaled_attention_softmax_v2 not found in kernel table"}

- 2025-02-18 09:30 - compared image digests / artifact tags:
  Canonical: gcr.io/redwood/frontend:v2025.02.14-rc2 (previous canary stable)
  New:       gcr.io/redwood/frontend:v2025.02.14-rc3 (this canary)
  $ docker image inspect gcr.io/redwood/frontend:v2025.02.14-rc3 | jq '.Id'\  
  "sha256:abcd1234..."

- 2025-02-18 09:35 - checked release notes for rc3: found kernel selection change + new op shim enabled (PR #789).
  PR link: https://github.com/repo/redwood-inference-deploys/pull/789

Hypotheses (initial):
1) New kernel selector / op shim in rc3 introduced an op name change (scaled_attention_softmax_v2) that the runtime kernel table on the canary nodes doesn't have (or the compiled kernels don't match the image).
2) Build artifact / image mismatch: nodes are running a different kernel runtime binary (old compiled kernels) while image references a new op name -> mismatch at runtime.
3) Config / feature-flag not propagated to all nodes (partial config causing mixed-mode execution).

Quick checks and commands run to verify hypotheses:
- Verified node images and rolling update status:
  $ kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=frontend-inference -o wide\  
  frontend-inference-canary-7f9d - IMAGE: gcr.io/redwood/frontend:v2025.02.14-rc3 - NODE: gpu-prod-12
  frontend-inference-574d - IMAGE: gcr.io/redwood/frontend:v2025.02.14-rc2 - NODE: gpu-prod-09
  -> Nodes are mixed (expected during canary).

- Exec'd into canary pod to check binary SHA and kernel table:
  $ kubectl -n prod exec -it frontend-inference-canary-7f9d -c runtime -- /bin/bash -c \"sha256sum /opt/runtime/bin/inference-runtime || true\"
  2b7f9e...  /opt/runtime/bin/inference-runtime
  $ strings /opt/runtime/bin/inference-runtime | grep scaled_attention_softmax || true
  (no matches)
  -> runtime binary in canary image does NOT contain the symbol.

- Checked build pipeline artifacts in GCS for rc3:
  gs://redwood-builds/frontend/v2025.02.14-rc3/
  - runtime-binary: inference-runtime-2b7f9e (matches container sha)
  - kernel-archive: kernels-v1.12.tar.gz (contains op list)
  $ tar -tzf kernels-v1.12.tar.gz | grep scaled_attention_softmax_v2 || true
  kernels/op_list.txt (contains scaled_attention_softmax_v2)
  -> Kernel archive in artifact bucket contains the op, but runtime binary inside container doesn't reference it.

Interpretation so far:
- Artifact bucket shows kernel archive with the new op, but container runtime binary in canary container lacks the symbol. Possible mismatch between which kernel archive is loaded at container startup vs what the runtime was compiled against. Could be build step ordering bug: runtime compiled before kernel tarball updated, but packaging used later kernel archive. Alternatively, entrypoint is loading kernels from a mounted emptyDir or from node-local cache (stale).

Rollback attempts and results:
- 2025-02-18 09:50 - tried soft rollback to previous tag for canary only (helm set canary.image.tag=v2025.02.14-rc2):
  $ helm upgrade frontend-inference ./charts/frontend --namespace prod --reuse-values --set canary.image.tag=v2025.02.14-rc2 --set canary.weight=2
  -> helm reported upgrade, pods restarted.
  Observed: errors cleared within ~30s, canary latency back to baseline.

- 2025-02-18 10:05 - promoting full rollback (revert release to rc2): decision meeting notes -> approved.
  Commands executed:
  $ kubectl -n prod set image deployment/frontend-inference frontend=gcr.io/redwood/frontend:v2025.02.14-rc2
  $ kubectl -n prod rollout status deployment/frontend-inference --timeout=5m
  Result: rollout healthy, no further 502s.

Notes on what likely happened (post-rollback quick analysis):
- Packaging pipeline for rc3 produced artifacts where kernel archive and runtime binary were out-of-sync. The artifact bucket shows kernel archive has op, but the binary in the container does not reference it, causing runtime to attempt to call op that isn't present -> upstream errors.
- The runtime has fallback behavior (slow cold path) which caused latency spikes when it hit the missing op path, and sometimes returned 502 when that failed.

Next steps / action items (TODOs):
- [ ] Block rc3 from redeploy until build pipeline fixed (remove rc3 tag from deployable list). Owner: Maya.
- [ ] Add a pre-deploy smoke-test that validates kernel-op presence for every new image (exec into image and run op-list check). Owner: Ethan.
- [ ] Add gated step in CD: verify runtime binary symbol table includes ops declared in kernel archive (or run small inference script to exercise op). Owner: Release CI team.
- [ ] Investigate build pipeline ordering: ensure kernel archive and runtime are built from same commit + packaging picks the correct artifacts. Owner: Liam.
- [ ] Add monitoring alert for operator-mismatch errors (\"op_not_found\" / \"upstream runtime error\") to SRE routing. Owner: eng-sre.
- [ ] Postmortem doc and timeline (formal) \u2014 link to draft postmortem and JIRA RI-3421. Owner: Maya/Ethan.

Notes to self (scratchpad):
- Could also be node-local cache: check DaemonSet that preloads kernels on hosts (gpu-preload). Maybe rc3 expected preload v1.12 but nodes still had v1.11. Check /var/cache/kernels on gpu nodes.
- If packaging order is the root cause, fix: make packaging deterministic (include build manifest with checksums of runtime & kernel tarball).
- For future canaries: increase smoke-test coverage (exercise a few operator-heavy paths).

Raw error snippets copied for postmortem:
- \"upstream runtime error: op_scaled_attention_softmax_v2 not found in kernel table\"
- runtime log sample:
  2025-02-18T09:22:03Z ERROR runtime - Failed to lookup op 'scaled_attention_softmax_v2' in op registry (key error)
  2025-02-18T09:22:03Z ERROR http.server - 502 upstream error - request_id=abc123

Manual rollback command history (for audit):
- 2025-02-18 09:50 helm rollback (canary to rc2) - helm upgrade with canary.image.tag override
- 2025-02-18 10:05 kubectl set image deployment/frontend-inference frontend=gcr.io/redwood/frontend:v2025.02.14-rc2

Open questions / unknowns:
- Did any other release also include the kernel change? cross-check with other services.
- Was there a race in the build CI where kernels were published after the runtime binary was compiled? Need build logs from CI-1093.
- Are we certain node-level preload isn't interfering? check gpu-preload daemonset logs (host-level).

If anyone reading: add anything I missed. Will turn this into the formal incident postmortem after we gather CI logs and daemonset state.

-- Maya
